qt: to the Council Özlem Demirel (The Left) Subject:

In 2017, as part of phase 1 of the SIBMMIL programme, the European Commission called on Italy to establish an EU-funded Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) in Libya. The money has been spent, but when I asked about it in 2021, neither the Council nor the Commission were able to say where this equipment is located. The Italian Ministry of the Interior has not been able to provide an explanation to journalists either. That same year, the EU launched phase 2 of the programme, and delivered an additional mobile, container-based MRCC. Various militias are now quarrelling over the equipment, meaning that it has yet to become operational. 1.
Where exactly is the equipment that was delivered under phase 1 of the SIBMMIL programme for a MRCC in Tripoli, and to what extent is this MRCC operating as planned?
If, in the Council’s view, the MRCC in Tripoli is not yet operational, what shortcomings need to be resolved, and what efforts is the Council making to this end?

Who is in charge of the container delivered in phase 2 of the SIBMMIL programme, and which Libyan units (coastal guard, navy, maritime police or other militias) are to operate them, in which location?
at: (English version) to the Council Özlem Demirel (The Left) (16 January 2024) Subject: Status and location of EU-funded Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre in Libya In 2017, as part of phase 1 of the SIBMMIL programme, the European Commission called on Italy to establish an EU-funded Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) in Libya. The money has been spent, but when I asked about it in 2021, neither the Council nor the Commission were able to say where this equipment is located. The Italian Ministry of the Interior has not been able to provide an explanation to journalists either. That same year, the EU launched phase 2 of the programme, and delivered an additional mobile, container-based MRCC. Various militias are now quarrelling over the equipment, meaning that it has yet to become operational. 1. Where exactly is the equipment that was delivered under phase 1 of the SIBMMIL programme for a MRCC in Tripoli, and to what extent is this MRCC operating as planned? 2. If, in the Council’s view, the MRCC in Tripoli is not yet operational, what shortcomings need to be resolved, and what efforts is the Council making to this end? 3. Who is in charge of the container delivered in phase 2 of the SIBMMIL programme, and which Libyan units (coastal guard, navy, maritime police or other militias) are to operate them, in which location? Reply (18 March 2024) The Council is following the implementation of the actions outlined in the action file on Libya within the framework of the Operational coordination mechanism for the external dimension of migration (MOCADEM). The aim of these actions is to further operationalise the EU Action Plan for the Central Mediterranean with regard to Libya, developing a holistic approach and identifying short and medium-term actions that can contribute to more effective Libyan border and migration management, prevent irregular departures, counter migrant smuggling and trafficking networks and reinforce search and rescue capacities. The specific information requested by the Honourable Member is not available to the Council. The Honourable Member is invited to put this question to the Commission.
